principle_1_harness_owns_the_books.name: The scorer never trusts the scored
principle_1_harness_owns_the_books.summary: Billing, token counts, SLO accounting and quality all come from the harness's private records; the router's copy of the fleet is published by value and diffed after every callback.
principle_1_harness_owns_the_books.tradeoff: Makes every number un-gameable, at the cost of a router being unable to learn from anything it was not explicitly handed.

principle_2_refusal_is_priced.name: Refusing work is priced, not free
principle_2_refusal_is_priced.summary: A shed request books zero quality, a quality-floor miss and a violated SLO, and is legal only when no provider could have served it right then.
principle_2_refusal_is_priced.tradeoff: Removes the degenerate 'drop the hard traffic' strategy, but makes a router that over-sheds during a burst worse than one that queues.

principle_3_waiting_is_also_losing.name: Waiting forever is a typed loss, not a stall
principle_3_waiting_is_also_losing.summary: Deferring a structurally unservable request past a 32-defer grace, or dispatching into an announced outage past an 8-attempt grace, is reported as losing the request rather than allowed to hang.
principle_3_waiting_is_also_losing.tradeoff: Forces a router to have an explicit give-up path; costs it the option of optimistically waiting out a long outage.

principle_4_announced_failure_beats_infe.name: Announce unavailability instead of making it inferable
principle_4_announced_failure_beats_infe.summary: A down provider publishes an empty catalogue and an ETA rather than merely erroring, so a correct router never has to estimate health from error rates.
principle_4_announced_failure_beats_infe.tradeoff: Simplifies the policy enormously, but only works where the fleet is cooperative; a real gateway must infer.

principle_5_one_slo_field_per_request.name: The request names which latency matters
principle_5_one_slo_field_per_request.summary: A request carries either ttft_ms or latency_ms and the harness measures exactly that quantity, so one policy can serve an interactive and a batch tenant without a mode switch.
principle_5_one_slo_field_per_request.tradeoff: Keeps the interface small; hides the fact that the two regimes want opposite placements on the same fleet.

principle_6_liveness_fails_loudly.name: A livelocked policy aborts, it does not grind
principle_6_liveness_fails_loudly.summary: Explicit per-request decide() and wall-clock budgets convert a non-progressing policy into a typed harness_hang with its own diagnostic instead of a hung test.
principle_6_liveness_fails_loudly.tradeoff: Bounds test time; a legitimately slow policy must be told the budget exists.
